solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing; clues and answers read from cryptics.georgeho.org (ODbL)'s copy of the post

clue.text: Share activity under the table?

definitions.meaning: the FTSE 100 index of London share prices, nicknamed after its initials, tracks share activity
the flirtatious game of touching feet hidden beneath a dining table

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether shares are being traded secretly, in a shady under-the-table deal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Under the table' suggests a bribe or illicit deal; here it is literal, the feet beneath the table. The FTSE index is the Financial Times Stock Exchange index, said as a word.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses share one sound: the stock index nickname for the FTSE, and flirting with the feet.

clue.text: Tiff upset leader deserting eager team

indicators.note: being upset means being knocked over, so the letters are disordered
the leading letter leaves the word

parts.note: keen means eager

explanation.surface: After a quarrel, the captain walks out on an enthusiastic side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leader deserting' looks like a team captain quitting, but drops the K from KEEN.
explanation.definitionFit: A rugby union side has fifteen players, so the number names the team.

clue.text: Couple among our number lived through…

indicators.note: set in the middle of the word that follows

parts.note: taken as written
a couple is two
e is the mathematical constant, a number

explanation.surface: A pair of our group survived something, continued into the next clue's siege.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis runs on into 3 down: lived through a blockade. E is Euler's number in mathematics.
explanation.definitionFit: To outwear something is to last beyond it, to survive or endure it.

clue.text: … blockade of south Belgian town — fifty lost

indicators.note: something lost is removed from the word

parts.note: Liège is a city in eastern Belgium
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: A Belgian town in the south is blockaded and fifty people are lost.
explanation.walkthrough: Liège loses its accent as well as its L.
explanation.definitionFit: A siege surrounds a town and cuts off supplies, which is a military blockade.

clue.text: Disaffected Red agents turned

indicators.note: turning things over changes their order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Communist spies became disillusioned and switched sides.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turned' suggests agents changing allegiance as double agents; it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone estranged has been alienated and no longer feels loyal or close, so disaffected.

clue.text: In meeting at Number Ten I backtracked somewhat

indicators.note: the setter lets backtracked lend its own letters and its sense, read in its backward direction; In here sends the run the other way
only some of the letters of these words are used, a run lying across them

parts.note: going back over the track means the run of letters is read from right to left

explanation.surface: Someone at a Downing Street meeting admits to having partly gone back on what they said.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Backtracked' does double duty: it signals the reversal and also supplies BAC, the end of the run TENIBAC read backwards. Number Ten Downing Street is the British Prime Minister's residence.
explanation.definitionFit: The senior ministers of the British government meet as a body in Downing Street, the Prime Minister's house.

clue.text: Tailless seal's hideaway

indicators.note: without its tail, the word loses its final letter

parts.note: a cachet is a seal stamped on a letter or document

explanation.surface: A seal with no tail retreats to its secret lair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Seal' looks like the animal, but is the stamp, CACHET.
explanation.definitionFit: A cache is a hidden store or hiding place, a secret stash.

clue.text: A convenience for the elderly — clothed or not?

definitions.text: A convenience for the elderly — clothed or not?

parts.words: A convenience for the elderly — clothed or not?
parts.note: an old-fashioned wheeled chair for invalids, whose name begins with a word for where you are unclothed

explanation.surface: A query whether an aid for old people is used dressed or undressed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Convenience' hints at a lavatory; it is a wheeled invalid chair named after the spa town of Bath, though the name suggests bathing undressed.
explanation.definitionFit: A hooded wheeled seat once used to carry invalids and older people about.

clue.text: Navy (raised in island, note) set forth…

indicators.note: in a down entry, raising a letter sends it up to the top of the word

parts.note: Arran is an island in the Firth of Clyde, Scotland
te is the seventh note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A sailor stationed on an island gives a formal account of events.
explanation.walkthrough: The N at the foot of ARRAN is lifted to the top, making NARRA. The blog could not resolve this one.
explanation.definitionFit: To set forth a story is to recount or relate it in detail.

clue.text: …for which reason Spain's in danger

indicators.note: placed inside the word for danger

parts.note: a threat is a danger or menace
E is the international vehicle code for Spain (España)

explanation.surface: Continued from the previous clue: this is why Spain is at risk.
explanation.definitionFit: An archaic adverb meaning on that account, because of that, or at that point.

clue.text: Well-trained players on time for fixture

parts.note: in good physical condition from training, i.e. fit
members of a team or pieces in a game are men

explanation.surface: A sports report: a well-drilled side turns up punctually for its match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fixture' looks like a sporting match, chiming with the players; it actually means a fitted item of furniture or equipment.
explanation.definitionFit: A fixture in a house is something fixed in place, a fitted piece of equipment.

clue.text: Old Bob shuns esoteric dancing club

indicators.note: avoiding something means leaving it out of the letters that follow
the remaining letters dance about into a new order

parts.note: a bob was the old British shilling, abbreviated S

explanation.surface: An elderly man named Bob avoids an obscure, arty dance club.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old Bob' looks like a person but is the pre-decimal shilling, S. ESOTERIC without S leaves EOTERIC, which 'dancing' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: A small exclusive circle of people sharing interests is a set or club.

clue.text: Exchequer's earliest revenue returns, covering one year's end, put England in clear!

indicators.note: the earliest letter of a word is its initial one
one piece wraps around the next, holding it within
turning back means the word for revenue is read in reverse

parts.note: tax is the revenue a government collects
taken as written

indicators.note: a word's end is its last letter

explanation.surface: A Treasury story: early tax receipts come back and clear England of blame.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Returns' looks like tax returns but signals reversal (XAT); 'covering' wraps it round ONE and R, and 'put England in' adds the final E.
explanation.definitionFit: To exonerate is to clear someone of blame or a charge, to absolve them.

clue.text: Criminals' pronounced obsession

indicators.note: said out loud, the name of the gangster brothers matches a word for a passion

parts.note: the Kray twins were notorious London gangsters of the 1960s

explanation.surface: Criminals have a marked fixation on something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pronounced' looks like an adjective meaning marked, but signals a homophone. Ronnie and Reggie Kray ran organised crime in London's East End.
explanation.definitionFit: A craze is a passing enthusiasm or mania, a widespread obsession.

clue.text: Lashings of Pernod regularly given to half-cut alcoholic

indicators.note: one piece is handed on to another, so they join end to end
cutting a word in half leaves just its second half here

parts.note: a wino is a drunk who favours cheap wine

indicators.note: taking every other letter of a word

explanation.surface: Plenty of Pernod is poured out at intervals for a tipsy drinker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Half-cut' looks like slang for tipsy, but it halves WINO to NO. The even letters of Pernod give END.
explanation.definitionFit: Lashings is an informal word for a great deal of something, as is the idiom meaning endlessly much.

clue.text: Peripheral joint is starting to keep medic indoors

indicators.note: set within the walls of the word for a joint

parts.note: a dive is a seedy bar or club, a disreputable joint
taken as written

indicators.note: the start of the next word, its first letter

parts.note: DR is the abbreviation for doctor

explanation.surface: A doctor is kept inside a dodgy outlying bar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Peripheral' looks like an adjective but is the noun for an add-on device of a computer.
explanation.definitionFit: A computer peripheral is an external device, such as a unit for reading storage media.

clue.text: Sponsor of series sadly pulled out in upheaval of Great Depression

indicators.note: a sad state of affairs mixes up the letters of the word before it
those letters are pulled out of the phrase that follows
an upheaval throws the remaining letters into a new order

explanation.surface: A sponsor withdraws backing from a TV series amid the economic chaos of the 1930s slump.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove the letters of SERIES from GREATDEPRESSION, leaving GATDPREON, then rearrange those.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who sponsors a child at baptism takes on the role of godparent.

clue.text: Invalidate ride managed in record time

parts.note: a disc is a gramophone record

indicators.note: something managed is handled and worked into a new shape

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A fairground ride run in record time is declared void.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Record' reads as a best-ever time but is a gramophone disc; 'managed' signals rearranging RIDE into REDI.
explanation.definitionFit: To discredit a theory or witness is to undermine it, robbing it of credibility.

clue.text: This thrice from disfavouring this?

parts.note: removing the outer letters of disfavouring three times over leaves favour, so doing it is what turns disfavour into favour, i.e. choosing a camp

explanation.surface: A riddle that refers to itself, asking what to do three times to a word.
explanation.walkthrough: Strip the outside letters of DISFAVOURING thrice (D-G, I-N, S-I) and FAVOUR remains: favouring one party is what the answer means.
explanation.definitionFit: To support one party in a dispute is to back one faction against another.

clue.text: Holding thrash, students periodically escalate disorder

indicators.note: one piece holds another inside it
in a down entry, escalating means going up, so the letters run bottom to top
taking letters at regular intervals

parts.note: to tan someone's hide is to thrash them

explanation.surface: Students hold a riot, and the disturbance escalates periodically.
explanation.walkthrough: Alternate letters of students give SUET; going up turns that to TEUS, which holds TAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Tetanus, or lockjaw, is a bacterial disease, a medical disorder.

clue.text: Congenial Mr Cutting from Kidderminster beaten up

indicators.note: cutting something from a word removes its letters
letters beaten up are knocked into a new order

parts.note: Mr is the abbreviation of mister

explanation.surface: A friendly Mr Cutting from Kidderminster has been assaulted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mr Cutting' looks like a name; remove MISTER from KIDDERMINSTER (a town in Worcestershire) to leave KIDDERN, then rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Kindred as an adjective means related or of like nature, hence sympathetic or congenial.

clue.text: Shown again as untrustworthy, unmarried servant sacked

indicators.note: letters that can't be trusted to stay put are rearranged
a sacked servant is removed, so those letters go from the word

parts.note: a maid is a female domestic servant

explanation.surface: An unreliable single servant is dismissed and shown the door again.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove MAID from UNMARRIED to leave UNRRE, then rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: A programme broadcast for a second time is a repeat screening.

clue.text: Multi-ethnic artists fashionable by inclination

parts.note: RA stands for Royal Academician, a member of the Royal Academy of Arts
in means in fashion
a bow is an inclination of the head or body

explanation.surface: Artists from many backgrounds are trendy because of their leanings.
explanation.definitionFit: South Africa's description of itself as the rainbow nation means a diverse, many-raced society.

clue.text: Celebrations in NY?

parts.note: the letters N and Y stand for the initials of the January 1 festival, not the city of New York

explanation.surface: A question about festivities in New York City.
explanation.walkthrough: 'NY' looks like New York, but is the abbreviation for the turn of the calendar.
explanation.definitionFit: The festivities held on the first of January mark the start of a fresh calendar period.

clue.text: Prepared the pitch and square with a French top dressing

parts.note: a T-square is a draughtsman's tool, so T can stand for square
une is French for a

indicators.note: the top of a word in an across entry is its first letter

explanation.surface: A groundsman readies the cricket pitch and square, then gives the turf a top dressing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pitch' suggests a sports ground (the square is the central strip of a cricket field); it means musical pitch, as for an instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: Adjusting an instrument so its notes are at the right musical pitch is preparing it.

clue.text: Endeavour might give you an outlook on life

definitions.meaning: the Space Shuttle Endeavour offers a view of the whole globe from orbit
a personal philosophy or general way of seeing things

explanation.surface: Effort, it is suggested, can give you a philosophy of life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Endeavour' reads as effort, but is the NASA space shuttle, from which the planet can be seen.
explanation.definitionFit: A comprehensive philosophy or perspective on existence, and literally a view of the globe.

clue.text: Mrs Beckham maybe's admitting quarter of earnings

indicators.note: letting something in, so it goes inside

parts.note: Victoria Beckham is the archetypal WAG, a footballer's wife or girlfriend in British tabloid slang
E for east, one of the four quarters of the compass

explanation.surface: A celebrity footballer's wife owns up to receiving a quarter of the income.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Quarter' looks like a fraction of the earnings, but is a compass point.
explanation.definitionFit: Wages are payments for work, regular earnings.

clue.text: Is his oeuvre rudimentary? Some raise it

definitions.text: Is his oeuvre rudimentary? Some raise it

indicators.note: in a down entry, raising the letters reads them from bottom to top
only part of these words is used, a run of letters inside them

explanation.surface: Critics question whether an artist's body of work is crude, and some raise it.
explanation.walkthrough: The German Renaissance engraver is hidden backwards in 'oeuvRE RUDimentary'; the clue as a whole asks about his work.
explanation.definitionFit: Albrecht Dürer was a German Renaissance painter and printmaker whose oeuvre is anything but basic.

clue.text: Train men to yodel — that's entertaining!

parts.note: the NUR was the National Union of Railwaymen in Britain
yodelling is a form of singing

explanation.surface: Teaching railwaymen to yodel would certainly be amusing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Entertaining' looks like 'amusing' but means harbouring, as in entertaining a hope or nursing a grudge.
explanation.definitionFit: To entertain an idea or feeling is to harbour or cherish it, as in nursing a grievance.

clue.text: Deserted old city on west-facing island is substantial…

parts.note: Ur was an ancient city of Mesopotamia

indicators.note: in an across entry, facing west means reading right to left

parts.note: Elba is the Mediterranean island where Napoleon was exiled

explanation.surface: An abandoned ancient city stands on a sturdy island looking west.
explanation.definitionFit: Something substantial is solidly made and long-lasting, built to last.

clue.text: …to south, notice promontory in the gloom

parts.note: an ad is a notice or advertisement
a ness is a headland, as in Scottish place names

explanation.surface: Going south, you spot a headland in the murky gloom.
explanation.definitionFit: Gloom is low spirits or melancholy, a state of unhappiness.

clue.text: Hot or wet, last of beer's swilled in pitcher

indicators.note: liquid swilled round is swirled about, so these letters are mixed

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hot on taps
taken as written
taken as written

indicators.note: the final letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: Beer is sloshed around in a jug whatever the weather.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pitcher' looks like a jug; it is one who throws, as in baseball.
explanation.definitionFit: A pitcher in baseball is the player who hurls the ball, one who throws.
